title: MatterSim and tantalum phosphide as a good heat conductor
summary: A candidate identified with MatterSim-v1, tetragonal tantalum phosphide, was synthesized and showed thermal conductivity of 152 W/m/K in the best samples, close to silicon. MatterSim-v1 inference is 3–5 times faster, and the new multi-task model MatterSim-MT predicts energies, forces, and properties. Battery and other property results are predictions, not experimental confirmations.

evidence.tested: A MatterSim-v1 screen of over 240,000 candidates picked tetragonal tantalum phosphide, which was synthesized at UT Dallas and whose thermal conductivity was measured at UIUC, reaching 152 W/m/K in the best samples; the page does not describe the measurement method or number of samples.
evidence.unknown: The page states that practical constraints such as mass density, elemental abundance and environmental stability are needed, but does not say whether TaP meets them.
evidence.ai_role: MatterSim-v1 machine-learning interatomic potentials estimated phonon thermal conductivity to screen candidates before experimental validation; MatterSim-MT is a multi-task model.
